ranked.headline: DESI-era data probe dynamical dark energy, early dark energy and primordial features
ranked.summary: New analyses pit w0wa, early dark energy and primordial-feature models against DESI BAO, Planck PR4, HSC-Y3 shear, FRBs and JWST galaxy counts.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is testing whether combined datasets prefer extensions of ΛCDM, chiefly dynamical dark energy. HSC-Y3 cosmic shear with DESI BAO, DES SNe and BBN priors yields a 2.4σ preference for time-varying w. Allowing w0wa removes the hinted early-recombination preference from CMB+BAO and gives the lowest AIC. A genetic-algorithm reconstruction of scalar-tensor Lagrangians improves on ΛCDM by Δχ²=-16.6. 125 localized FRBs alone constrain Ω_m and w for the first time. A Bayesian forecast asks whether Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 can separate w0waCDM from ΛCDM shadow models. On H0, a double-power scalar field unifies early and late dark energy, and axion EDE with JWST high-redshift galaxy abundances gives H0≈72.76 km/s/Mpc. Searches for axion monodromy and full-shape BOSS/eBOSS oscillatory features find no significant evidence. Updated CMB acoustic priors separate early-Universe information from lensing and ISW. Separately, NANOGrav binary pulsars constrain ultralight dark matter couplings.

ranked.headline: Hybrid bias models, marked statistics and systematics sharpen survey-era cosmology
ranked.summary: New hybrid EFT models, marked statistics and light-cone systematics studies target DESI, Euclid, LSST and Simons Observatory analyses beyond the power spectrum.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the modelling of tracer bias and non-Gaussian information for upcoming large-scale-structure analyses. Hybrid Lagrangian bias expansions are extended to post-reconstruction clustering, where a joint pre- and post-reconstruction analysis improves cosmological constraints. They are also extended to diffuse baryons via N-body displacements, a Lorentzian feedback suppression and linear bias. On primordial non-Gaussianity, a subhalo abundance matching model fit to small-scale clustering, combined with separate-universe simulations, constrains b_φ. Separately, neglecting light-cone and relativistic effects biases local fNL by ~2σ for a Euclid-like survey and by >10σ for a MegaMapper-like survey. Marked statistics appear in two forms: luminosity-weighted marks as a null test for assembly bias in DESI-BGS mocks, and rotation-equivariant neural marks that extract information beyond the power spectrum. Other contributions include CosmoMap, a 3D U-Net mapping dark matter to gas temperature and electron density, and lensing ratios as geometric probes of dark energy and curvature for LSST and Simons Observatory.

ranked.headline: Magic-state certification and sharper information-theoretic bounds for qubit systems
ranked.summary: Three new preprints give certification criteria for nonstabilizerness, alongside tighter capacity, entropy and recovery-map bounds for qubit channels and states.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the operational characterization of nonstabilizerness (magic) in multi-qubit systems. One preprint certifies magic from few copies using moments of the discrete Wigner function. Another uses a stabilizer pigeonhole criterion with worst-case random access codes, covering states including W states. A third proves that multi-qubit bound magic exists, meaning states that cannot be distilled to pure magic, via a PPT-like criterion closed under tensor products. A second thread tightens quantitative bounds in quantum Shannon theory. These include a two-way-assisted capacity upper bound for amplitude-damping channels that is strictly tighter than PLOB, and sharp purity-based continuity bounds for von Neumann entropy with machine-learning-assisted estimation. A semidefinite-programming framework unifies pretty good measurements and Petz recovery maps. Separately, the classical complexity of state transmission is identified with the classical communication needed to simulate quantum correlations.

ranked.headline: Trotter scheduling, classical surrogates and early-FTQC estimators target simulation cost
ranked.summary: New Trotter variants, classical fermionic and spin-bath simulators, and a sampling-efficient energy-difference algorithm sharpen quantum simulation tooling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is reducing the cost of simulating quantum dynamics, on quantum hardware and classically. On the circuit side, one preprint schedules sub-Hamiltonians in Trotter decomposition by combining simultaneous diagonalization with higher-order Trotter-Suzuki ideas. Another builds an integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for unitary integration of nonlinear dynamics, applied to the Stepanoff flow. An early-FTQC algorithm estimates small energy differences such as molecular forces directly from dynamics, with lower sampling cost than phase estimation. Classical counterparts are also prominent. Dirac propagation simulates local fermionic observables under particle-number-conserving unitaries. Cluster spin-LSC treats a sensor and strongly coupled bath spins quantum mechanically to model spin-qubit decoherence. A polynomial-cost effective Hamiltonian method models couplings in 96-transmon processors and predicts 100-qubit quench dynamics. Separately, a hybrid framework uses simulated annealing and quantum-assisted ground-state estimation to find compact bases for ab initio many-fermion problems. Explicit symmetry adaptation is less central than in earlier work; particle-number conservation in Dirac propagation is the closest case.

ranked.headline: Decoders and simulators adapt to qubit loss, leakage and full circuit-level noise
ranked.summary: New tools target loss, leakage and circuit-level noise directly: loss-aware decoders, exact loss simulation, non-binary error models and GPU qLDPC decoding.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is modeling and decoding realistic circuit-level faults beyond i.i.d. Pauli noise. For qubit loss, Ellis uses frame-CSS certification to give exact, fast Pauli-frame shot sampling. A loss-aware CNN decoder with a fast sampler substantially reduces logical error rates for surface and high-rate qLDPC codes. Foliated surface codes are shown optimal against space- and time-like skip-gate leakage, outperforming SWAP-based circuits in stability. On the decoding side, non-binary detector error models merge Pauli error components to improve belief propagation. A GPU decoder for bivariate bicycle codes sustains one syndrome round per microsecond under circuit-level noise, with 120x throughput. A secondary thread concerns logical operations: code quilts enable ancilla-free fault-tolerant Pauli-product measurements between codeblocks. CSS-T-Product codes realize multi-qubit logical diagonal gates transversally, which enables tailored magic-state factories for algorithmic primitives.

ranked.headline: Foundation models, emulators and benchmarks are being built for survey-scale cosmological inference
ranked.summary: Euclid, Rubin, SPHEREx and SKA-era pipelines are being benchmarked and automated, with SDC3b exposing inter-team variability in EoR inference.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the construction and validation of inference components for Euclid, Rubin, SPHEREx and SKA-era data. Self-supervised models are applied to imaging: EuclidFM learns 128-dim source embeddings from Euclid Q1 photometry, and JAISP fuses ten-band Rubin and Euclid imaging for detection and astrometry. Lens-Orchestra uses multimodal LLM agents to automate forward modeling of 185 Euclid Q1 lens candidates. On the systematics and emulation side, SPHEREx clustering uses information-criterion-driven non-linear deprojection tested on lognormal mocks, symbolic regression diagnoses a Lyman-alpha GP emulator, and a differentiable GPU-accelerated forward model targets 21-cm uncertainty quantification. SDC3b reports inter-team variability among 16 EoR pipelines, underscoring the need for cross-method validation. The items span different observables and methods.

ranked.headline: Search and solver-based synthesis optimizes fault-tolerant and algorithmic quantum circuits
ranked.summary: Six preprints apply constraint solving, tree search, LLM-driven search and verified compilation to cut circuit cost across error-correction and algorithm layers.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is automated, search-based design of quantum circuits under explicit cost or correctness constraints. For fault tolerance, Block Checks with Pareto tree search target depth-operation trade-offs in state preparation, while CP-SAT synthesis exploits code structure to lower logical error rates in syndrome extraction for CSS quantum LDPC codes. At the algorithm level, LLM-driven search redesigns the approximate RNS modular exponentiation pipeline for RSA-2048, reducing expected Toffoli count by up to 78.6%. QBlue is extended to block-encoding algorithms with machine-checked verification, evaluated on 279 programs against PennyLane. Structure-aware compilation for independent-set optimization and context-aware variational synthesis with mid-circuit reconstruction complete the picture. The novelty lies in coupling optimization with structural or formal guarantees, though the preprints address different circuit classes.

ranked.headline: Noisy mediators, parallel transversal gates and measurement-free correction are proposed for fault-tolerant control
ranked.summary: New preprints propose mediator-based and transversal gates, measurement-free error correction, and improved readout across ion, cavity, atom and spin platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is control and error-management design for multi-qubit operations across platforms, with all items being preprints. One proposes reset-assisted control in which noisy mediator qubits drive high-fidelity gates on long-lived data qubits, analyzed with quantum trajectories. Another proposes parallel transversal controlled-Z gates across neighboring wells in a double-well trapped-ion architecture, with dynamical decoupling and crosstalk treatment. A measurement-free protocol for superconducting cavities corrects single-photon loss without syndrome readout. Supporting items address confidence-aware readout of 171Yb tweezer arrays, which matches fidelity with half the imaging time, a phonon-aware Lindblad model of electron-to-nuclear spin transfer in NV centers, and a review of qudit control across several platforms. Most results are proposals or simulations rather than experimental demonstrations.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-exploiting and tensor-network methods scale many-body simulation and state preparation
ranked.summary: Six preprints extend classical tensor-network, symmetry, and Pauli-propagation methods to larger fermionic, chemical, thermal, and scar-state problems.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on classical structure, such as symmetry, tensor-network form, and learned or propagated representations, to make many-body problems tractable at larger scale or lower quantum cost. NN-GPEPS combines neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks for strongly correlated fermions, reporting state-of-the-art Hubbard energies. Two papers load DMRG matrix product states onto hardware by exploiting spin symmetry: abelian block-sparse protocols, with Toffoli counts cut up to 135x, and non-Abelian SU(2) reduction via Wigner-Eckart and Clebsch-Gordan transforms. PP-VarQITE pairs Pauli propagation with variational imaginary time for shallow thermal-state circuits on up to 98 qubits. Further items cover machine-learned scaling of holographic circuits and unified preparation of scar states from Dicke states.

ranked.headline: Classical training and learned priors steer quantum generative circuits and circuit design
ranked.summary: Five preprints use classical training, inference or latent search around quantum circuits, covering ground-state samplers, Hamiltonian learning and circuit transfer.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a hybrid pattern in which classical learning machinery trains, guides or designs quantum circuits, and the sampling of noisy circuits is not their central subject. A hypernetwork maps Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles for ground-state samplers, with shared training and local fine tuning. JEPA-based world models infer Hamiltonian parameters from measured few-body dynamics and recover Ising and Heisenberg chains. QPAT uses a Quantum Circuit Born Machine as a generative prior for classical LSTM, CNN and Transformer training. LatentRL-QAS transfers circuit designs across qubit counts via a circuit VAE and latent-space reinforcement learning. A fully quantum Transformer with non-unitary circuits and training without backpropagation is the most speculative proposal. The common new element is amortizing circuit parameterization or training across tasks rather than optimizing each instance separately.

ranked.headline: Analog and digital simulators probe strongly correlated lattice, gauge and open-system phases
ranked.summary: Five preprints from 23–24 November 2026 pair simulation platforms with spectroscopic or numerical probes of interacting many-body phases and dynamics.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on characterizing interacting quantum many-body systems through simulation and structured probes. Cold-atom work reports coherent meson-baryon conversion in a 1D SU(2) quantum link model and proposes site-resolved, lattice-modulation signatures of a rung-Mott insulator in bosonic two-leg ladders. A hybrid qubit-boson Trotterized circuit simulates Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard dynamics, benchmarked against exact diagonalization. Quantum Monte Carlo for 2D dipolar excitons yields an analytical framework for chemical potential and interaction energies. Liouvillian quasiparticle spectroscopy extends spectral concepts to open systems, with protocols and numerical validation. The novelty lies in pairing each system with a measurable observable or benchmark rather than in a single shared method; the connection to concurrence or graph spectra is not evident from these summaries.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-derived transport and Hall responses predicted for odd-parity, p-wave and polar layered materials
ranked.summary: New first-principles and symmetry analyses tie odd-parity magnetism and stacking or polarization order to measurable charge, spin, valley and thermal responses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is theory that links measurable responses to symmetry-defined order. For odd-parity magnets, charge-spin selection rules and temporal-spectral separation are proposed as general transport signatures. In twisted bilayer NiPS3, a perpendicular electric field is predicted to reorient p-wave spin textures. Related first-principles work extends to polar and stacking order: shift current in hexagonal boron nitride multilayers tracks stacking and polarization, and sliding antiferroelectric four-layer MoS2 is predicted to host a quantum-metric-driven nonlinear valley Hall effect. Axial ferrons in uniaxial ferroelectrics are predicted to show thermal and angular-momentum Hall effects. What is new is the shared emphasis on electric-field or stacking tunability and on symmetry-based selection rules. All five items are preprints, and the predictions remain untested experimentally.

ranked.headline: Moiré and substrate coupling tune polaritons, phonons and flatbands in graphene and THz structures
ranked.summary: Five preprints report gate-tunable polaritons, moiré electron-phonon Fano coupling, chiral phonons and flatbands, showing coupling engineering in layered platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is engineering of hybrid excitations in graphene-based layered systems, with moiré structure as the main control parameter. Twisted bilayer graphene hosts hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons with gate-tunable wavelengths, studied from AB stacking to 5.5°. In graphene/hBN superlattices, a Fano resonance is reported as the first direct observation of coupling between moiré flat-band electronic excitations and hBN out-of-plane optical phonons. Helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy reveals reconfigurable chiral phonons in asymmetrically stacked moiré superlattices. Two works extend the theme to related structures: hybrid plasmon-phonon eigenmodes forming vortex states in a graphene ring on silica, and high-Q collective flatbands with zero group velocity in hybrid Mie-grating THz metasurfaces. The new element is direct spectroscopic evidence of moiré-mediated interlayer coupling alongside demonstrated tunability.

ranked.headline: Stacking order, displacement fields and driving reshape valley and topological bands in graphene
ranked.summary: Five preprints tie stacking, displacement field or Floquet driving to valley polarization, topological bands and superconductivity in graphene multilayers.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is that stacking geometry, gating and external driving set the low-energy band structure and valley character of graphene multilayers. In ABA trilayer graphene, a displacement field inverts band edges, reverses Berry curvature and produces valley splitting. In 17-layer rhombohedral graphene, superconductivity is reported with valley-imbalanced Fermi pockets and is enhanced by in-plane field. In twisted monolayer-N-layer rhombohedral graphene, narrow topological bands arise from hybridization of Dirac cone and surface states, with layer number as a control. Floquet driving of twisted bilayer heterostructures is predicted to yield valley polarization and Chern-number transitions, while a study of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene finds hidden f-wave TIVC order near nu=-2. The items are all preprints, and the evidence does not establish a single mechanism across these systems.

ranked.headline: Hall responses arise from orbital order, disorder and interactions without spin magnetism
ranked.summary: Five preprints trace Hall responses to orbital exchange, disorder, 3D Chern-number limits and pseudospin order in Bernal graphene, including hysteretic transitions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that Hall-type responses are attributed to orbital degrees of freedom, disorder and interactions rather than to spin magnetism or pristine band topology alone. Reported results include orbital Hall currents generated by structural and electrostatic disorder, including in amorphous graphene, and intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity from an orbital exchange field in spinless monolayer H-phase MoS2 without spin-orbit coupling. In 3D quantum anomalous Hall systems built from coupled Weyl semimetals, Chern numbers alone fail to characterize chiral behavior. In Bernal multilayer graphene, Hartree-Fock work predicts anomalous Hall metals from pseudospin ordering in the tetralayer, while experiments on the pentalayer show displacement-field-tunable first-order transitions with hysteretic Hall responses. What is new is treating disorder and orbital or pseudospin order as sources of Hall responses.

ranked.headline: Particle-physics models of dark matter and baryogenesis confronted with theoretical and phenomenological bounds
ranked.summary: Four preprints sharpen dark-sector and early-Universe model tests via UV bounds, Boltzmann treatments, axion abundance and flavor-testable flavons.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on stress-testing early-Universe and dark-sector scenarios against consistency conditions or experimental reach. Dirac leptogenesis is extended to charged leptons in a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, with a 1.7-50 GeV flavon testable through lepton flavor observables. UV-complete models are used to bound inflationary parity violation from dynamical Chern-Simons terms, with strong bispectrum constraints. Higgs-portal dark matter near resonance is revisited by solving the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation, which indicates that standard treatments are inadequate beyond kinetic equilibrium. Multi-component axion dark matter with stochastic mixing allows QCD axions or ultralight ALPs to dominate the abundance and enlarges the allowed QCD axion parameter space. The new element is more rigorous treatment of each model's assumptions.

ranked.headline: DESI, JWST and HSC surveys map structure and baryons across cosmic time
ranked.summary: New DESI, JWST and HSC-SSP datasets provide structure, lensing and baryon-content measurements that can feed into cosmological tests, though none constrain dark energy directly.
ranked.synthesis: The previous dark-energy framing is not supported by the current items: none fits or constrains an extended dark-energy model. The common thread is survey-based mapping of structure across cosmic time. DESI DR1 physical quasar pairs at z≈2 trace protocluster environments, consistent with ΛCDM mock predictions. VENUS provides strong-lensing models for 57 JWST clusters with 1733 multiply-imaged systems and mass scaling relations. Localized FRBs crossmatched with DESI galaxy groups show a tentative 143 pc cm^-3 excess dispersion measure for group-intersecting sight lines, a baryon probe at low significance. The HSC-SSP spectroscopic search finds the Little Red Dot number density falling ~35x from z~4-8 to z~2.1-2.6 with a non-evolving luminosity-function knee. These are astrophysical and structural inputs, not dark-energy tests.

ranked.headline: Public pipelines for halo occupation, voids, N-body and forward-modelled photometry mature
ranked.summary: New code releases and validation tests cover HOD fitting, void finding, N-body convergence and differentiable SPHEREx photometry ahead of Stage IV surveys.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a methodological focus on the infrastructure connecting dark matter structure to survey observables. SciPIC-lite provides a public, flexible Halo Occupation Distribution pipeline for clustering observables. PhotoNs-3 is tested against GADGET for accuracy and convergence in power spectra, halo profiles and mass functions at Stage IV requirements, bearing on the simulated dark matter backbone onto which galaxies are painted. The Popcorn Void Finder reimplementation documents the algorithm and reports a change from a power-law to a Schechter-like void size function. Hesperos and Eosphoros add a differentiable forced-photometry operator and forward model for SPHEREx spectrophotometry. The new element is emphasis on reproducibility, validation and differentiability rather than new astrophysical results; the items address different stages of the pipeline and are not a single analysis chain.

ranked.headline: Spherical-collapse simulations show w(a) and sound speed do not fix clustering dark energy
ranked.summary: Two preprints use nonlinear spherical collapse to show background and linear dark energy parametrizations leave clustering underdetermined.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is nonlinear clustering as a discriminator of dark energy models that share the same background and linear description. One preprint argues that w(a) and a linear sound speed do not fully specify dark energy, and spherical-collapse simulations find central dark-energy behavior that differs between models. A companion preprint introduces a fully nonlinear fluid method that splits the dark energy action into kinetic and potential parts and tests it with spherical-collapse simulations. The new element is this action-level nonlinear treatment as a route to breaking degeneracies. The other two preprints address early-Universe physics: vector perturbations sourced by shear viscosity in warm inflation, and gravitational wave spectra from slowly evolving sources. They are only loosely connected to this thread.

ranked.headline: Field-level emulators and expansion-history mappings extend simulations to new regimes
ranked.summary: Four preprints extend simulation validation: a Lyman-alpha emulator, w(z) mapping onto constant-w runs, and wave-phase resolution criteria for scalar-field dark matter.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is extending the reach of expensive simulations through field-level mappings validated against reference runs. One paper trains a 3D U-Net to map density and velocity fields to Lyman-alpha flux, reproducing P1D, bispectrum and trispectrum across IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO. Two papers show that N-body dynamics depend on the expansion history a(τ), so constant-w simulations can reproduce CPL and general w(z) models, with power spectra agreeing within 0.2% in one case. A fourth builds matched LCDM-SFDM initial conditions linking CLASS-SFDM, MUSIC and AxioNyx, and finds that accurate density recovery does not guarantee adequate wave-phase resolution. New relative to the prior synthesis is the dark-matter initial-condition validation; the CAMELS gas emulator and DESI-BGS assembly-bias test are not in the current items.

ranked.headline: Gain-loss balance and coupling asymmetry control non-Hermitian spectral structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints identify specific coupling and gain-loss knobs that set BIC merging, symmetry breaking, and eigenstate splitting.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of gain-loss balance and coupling asymmetry as control parameters for non-Hermitian spectral structure. The four preprints identify different knobs and constraints. A four-mode model of C2-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs links coupling sign to BIC merging, Q~k^-6 scaling, and flatband formation. A analysis of time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with T symmetry finds that gain-loss induced symmetry breaking is forbidden, even for random gain-loss distributions. Pseudo-altermagnetism shows that balanced gain and loss can mimic altermagnetic spin splitting, with movable nodal structures. Tunable nonreciprocal coupling near a second-order polarization exceptional point produces state-selective eigenstate splitting, with one branch distinguished. What is new is the specific set of control mechanisms and constraints rather than a single unified result.

ranked.headline: Dynamic tuning of quasi-BIC resonances in liquid-crystal and WS2 metasurfaces
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report active tuning of quasi-BIC resonances, excitonic strong coupling in bulk WS2, and strain-driven terahertz modulation in crystals.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is controlling resonant response in nanophotonic structures through mode coupling and the surrounding environment. Two items address quasi-bound states in the continuum: a symmetric silicon metasurface embedded in a nematic liquid crystal, whose anisotropy-induced quasi-BICs are actively tunable, and bulk WS2 metasurfaces in which Brillouin-zone-folding quasi-BICs self-hybridize with A excitons into polarization-independent strong coupling. A review of terahertz phase modulation via strain in piezoelectric and nonlinear optical crystals addresses a related goal of dynamic control through a different physical route. The MXene-derived TiO2 polarizer on silicon photonics is a device-level result that sits at the edge of this thread. What is new is active spectral control via liquid-crystal integration and excitonic strong coupling in bulk material. All four items are preprints.

ranked.headline: Spatiotemporal structure programs polarization topology and coherence in classical light
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend explicit spatiotemporal design from polarization topology to joint control of topology, coherence and temporal structure in classical fields.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of spatiotemporal structure as a programmable degree of freedom for classical light, with polarization as the carried quantity. The vectorial spatiotemporal wavepackets construct polarization-encoded topological knots whose Stokes trajectories are linked and knotted. Two space-time metasurface studies program coherence: one synthesizes coherent polarization states into programmable quantum-inspired bits, and the other realizes Bell- and GHZ-like multipartite states in classical electromagnetic waves. The graphene optoelectronic metasurface shares the vectorial-topology theme, generating and tuning toroidal terahertz pulses through transient vectorial photocurrents, but it does not use the same programming route. What is new is the extension of explicit spatiotemporal design from polarization topology alone to joint control of topology, coherence and temporal structure in classical fields.

ranked.headline: Lattice topological phases classified by generalized symmetries and invariants
ranked.summary: Recent preprints redefine protecting symmetries and invariants for lattice topological phases, including on fractal geometries.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is symmetry-constrained classification of lattice topological phases, in which the protecting symmetry or invariant is generalized. One study identifies phases protected by half-chiral symmetry, where chiral symmetry acts on one sublattice only, and characterizes them with real-space invariants and zero-energy modes. A second generalizes the spectral localizer to unify Z and Z2 invariants for hinge modes, Dirac nodes and valley boundary modes. A third realizes SSH, Haldane, Qi-Wu-Zhang and Z2 insulators on fractal lattices, including site-eliminated, projected and patterned constructions. What is new is the widening of protecting symmetries and invariants rather than a single shared method, with the fractal study transferring established models while the others redefine the controlling symmetry or invariant.

ranked.headline: Theory proposals for superconducting and Josephson quantum transport devices
ranked.summary: Four preprints offer design predictions for phase-coherent superconducting transport, none yet backed by experimental demonstration.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is phase-coherent quantum transport, in which superconducting or Josephson elements control charge, spin and thermal responses. One preprint derives a lower bound on current noise in coherent electron transport via Floquet-Nambu scattering and a Cramér-Rao inequality. A numerical study proposes a flux-driven DC-SQUID threshold detector with nonequilibrium phase dynamics to reduce thermal noise and detect microwave pulses near the single-microwave-photon energy scale. A two-orbital quantum dot Josephson junction with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting maps a temperature difference onto a phase difference for thermometry. A theory proposal argues that the inverse spin Hall effect in a superconductor could approach unity spin-to-charge conversion in a nonlocal spin-valve geometry. All four items are preprints and theoretical or numerical proposals, so the new content consists of design predictions rather than experimental demonstrations.

ranked.headline: Computational optical imaging recovers information from limited or mixed measurements
ranked.summary: Four preprints from late November 2026 apply targeted computational or engineered fixes to specific acquisition bottlenecks in optical imaging.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these four preprints is the recovery of optical information from measurements that are imperfect or resource-limited, addressed either by computational processing or by engineered acquisition. In single-pixel imaging, a unified calibration and composite-readout framework treats temporal mixing as a measurement resource rather than a nuisance. Event-camera Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy uses continuous birefringent interferometer scanning to reach real-time widefield spectral acquisition. MCP-based EUV ptychography applies physics-simulation-trained residual learning to restore diffraction patterns, reporting an edge-response width of about 1.08 μm at 57 nm. The fourth item, a surrogate-guided design of incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks for onboard satellite image classification, is design-oriented rather than a reconstruction method. What is new in each item is a targeted treatment of a specific error source or resource bottleneck, although the modalities differ considerably.

ranked.headline: Tunable control of spin, photonic, acoustic and mechanical waves in confined resonators
ranked.summary: Recent preprints demonstrate phase-controlled spin waves, wireless magnon-polariton readout, and acoustic and nanomechanical nonlinearity control.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is control of confined spin, photonic, acoustic and mechanical waves through transducers, coupling geometry and nonlinearity. Two preprints use transducers and coupling to set wave behaviour: a VCMA open-resonator transducer provides two controlled phase states for parametric spin-wave excitation with a lowered threshold, and two wirelessly coupled ring resonators enable remote excitation and readout of cavity magnon-polaritons through photonic modes delocalised across a gap. The acoustic study, a 3D-printed labyrinthine meta-atom in a waveguide, relies on symmetry breaking in its bound states in the continuum, while the buckled nanotube resonator shows strong intrinsic nonlinearity, with bistability bounded at 34 phonons and a suggested approach to the single-phonon Kerr regime. The items differ in platform and maturity and do not all share one mechanism. What is new is the emphasis on phase-selective and remote addressing of spin and photonic modes, together with nonlinear mechanical resonators approaching few-phonon operation.

ranked.headline: Electronic models extended to fields, long-range terms and electron-phonon coupling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend electronic-structure models to external fields, long-range interactions and exciton-phonon workflows in large-scale simulations.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a computational focus on electronic states and their coupling to other degrees of freedom, rather than a single physical model. MLEH-LR, a machine-learning electronic Hamiltonian, adds long-range interactions and external fields and is applied to boron nitride ribbons. LeIFF treats valence electrons as dynamical spherical charge distributions in a compact force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics at large scale. LetzElPhC, an open-source code, computes electron-phonon and exciton-phonon matrix elements from DFPT output of Quantum ESPRESSO and interfaces with Yambo. The new element across the set is the extension of electronic-structure descriptions to external fields, long-range terms and phonon-coupled exciton workflows, implemented through learned or reduced models and efficient codes.

ranked.headline: Embedding wave propagation physics into neural inverse design and optical tomography
ranked.summary: Learned models now embed wave propagation physics to address broadband diffractive design and amplitude estimation in tomography.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the embedding of explicit physics into learned models for optical inverse problems. MSWNets couple fully connected networks with Rayleigh-Sommerfeld propagation in a PINN-inspired formulation to design broadband diffractive optics. Gradient optical diffraction tomography uses physics-informed deep learning, with a ResNet, to estimate the missing amplitude gradient, extending gradient-based tomography to amplitude retrieval. The high-harmonic study applies AI-assisted analysis to retrieve anisotropic nonlinear responses and crystal symmetries of atomically thin materials, a different regime of nonlinear light-matter interaction that shares only the learning-for-inference element. Across the two diffractive items, what is new is that propagation physics is built into the learning or estimation step itself.

ranked.headline: Nonlinear and non-Hermitian cavity schemes for quantum state control and sensing
ranked.summary: Recent preprints propose analytic and Floquet-based control of photon statistics and mechanical modes in coupled cavity systems.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a common thread: engineering coherent control in driven, coupled cavity systems through tailored nonlinearity, dissipation, or sideband driving. One study derives analytic optimal conditions for unconventional photon blockade in coupled cavities with second-order nonlinearity and asymmetric dissipation, targeting robust antibunching. A second proposes a Floquet sideband method to manipulate mechanical dark modes in a three-mode optomechanical system, supported by fidelity and population analyses. The third applies PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics with second-order sidebands and tunable slow-fast light to magnetometry, reporting theoretical picotesla-level sensitivity. The common element is the use of nonlinear terms, asymmetric dissipation, Floquet driving, and PT symmetry as explicit control parameters. All listed works are theoretical, and the summaries do not report experimental validation.

ranked.headline: Computational frameworks advance light propagation and structured-light tomography
ranked.summary: Efficient nonparaxial propagation and high-dimensional mode tomography are now validated against analytic and experimental benchmarks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational treatment of optical field propagation and characterization beyond standard paraxial or idealized assumptions. The Python Fourier-optics framework (arxiv:2611.25116) is benchmarked against analytic Gaussian beam, lens, and grating results, providing a checked simulation tool. The tilted-lens study (arxiv:2611.25427) extends intensity-based spatial mode tomography through an astigmatic transformation and reports fidelity at mode dimension D=66. The convolution-based formulation (arxiv:2611.27232) provides an efficient wide-angle, nonparaxial description of partially coherent light from extended incoherent sources, with absolute radiometric quantities. The common novelty is methodological: each work makes higher-dimensional or less restrictive optical models computationally accessible while checking results against known solutions or measurements.

ranked.headline: Multiple optical degrees of freedom are used to encode and recover information
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report six-dimensional optical storage, snapshot infrared sensing and 250 kHz wavefront shaping through multimode fibers.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of multiple optical degrees of freedom, spanning polarization, spectral and spatial information, to encode or control light beyond simple intensity. A six-dimensional storage scheme uses polarized light in laser-induced nanostructures and reports 99.45% raw accuracy. Gradient metasurface pixels map spectral and polarization content into spatial patterns for snapshot infrared optical sensing. A phase-only MEMS modulator with 8,192 elements and 250 kHz refresh performs wavefront shaping through multimode fiber, reporting 70% light delivery. The applications differ, so the dominant thread is multidimensional readout and control rather than a single shared method. The new element across these preprints is the pairing of pixelated polarization-spectral encoding with fast, high-element-count phase modulation.
